web.notes: The tag `tanrei-select`, the class `TanreiSelect` and the React name `Select` are the bare control, without the frame. Lagging: the element still draws the label row, the requirement mark and the supporting row itself. A form-associated custom element (`static formAssociated = true`): it takes `name`, submits `value`, restores it on navigation (`formStateRestoreCallback`), resets to the value it was first given, follows `<fieldset disabled>` and reports `valueMissing` while the Field that frames it says it is required and `value` is empty. Its two calls on `ElementInternals` and its form go through the shared field primitives, so that a select field can repeat them. The trigger is a `<div role="combobox" tabindex="0">` in the shadow root carrying the name, the description, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `aria-readonly`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` — set on that element, not through ElementInternals, which axe cannot see. The name and the description are values the Field gives (`tanrei-field-connect`, `src/primitives/field.ts`), written into the select's own shadow root, the select's own `label` winning; the connection runs in both directions (SEL-63): the control's side says `drawsLabel`, `inset: { start, end }` (lengths the select writes from its own tokens and its measured icon box) and `drawnFocused` (true while the list is open), and takes `labelHidden` and `requiredMark` (`asterisk` or `none`) beside the name, the description and the three states. A select that a Field frames is a block that fills the Field's width (SEL-49); a bare one is an inline box as wide as its widest option, measured from a hidden grid cell that stacks every option's label in the value's style. The options are `<tanrei-option>` and `<tanrei-option-group>` elements, read as data and never drawn in place: the select renders the rows itself in its shadow root, so that the combobox, its `aria-controls` listbox and its `aria-activedescendant` option are in one tree. It reads them from its own children, and — in `src/primitives/option-list.ts`, for the combobox too — through any `<slot>` among its children: the elements assigned to that slot, flattened, stand in the slot's place, in order. That is how a select field's options, which are the product's children of `<tanrei-select-field>`, reach the select inside it, and how a product's own element can pass options on. Changes are observed on the children, on each such slot (`slotchange`) and on each element assigned through one. The list is a manual popover in the top layer, placed with CSS anchor positioning and a script fallback and followed with the `FollowController` the menu uses, with the select's own light dismiss so that `toggle` carries a reason; a press outside also reaches the element under it. The select sets its own `value` before firing `change` (a composed, bubbling Event, as a native select's) and its own `open` before firing `toggle`, a CustomEvent whose `detail` holds `open` and `reason` — which is composed and not bubbling (the shipped element's is not yet): composed so that it is heard on a select field, not bubbling so that an ancestor's own `toggle` listener, a `<details>`'s, never hears a select's. Attributes: `label-hidden`, `readonly`, `clear-label`, the rest as the properties. The `leading-icon` slot is a named slot. Parts: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label` (the floating label), `requirement-label` (its asterisk), `value`, `placeholder`, `leading-icon`, `clear-button`, `chevron`, `list`, `option`, `option-label`, `option-supporting-text`, `option-leading-icon`, `mark`, `group`, `group-title`, `divider`, `status`. The status row (SEL-68, SEL-69) is a `<div part="status">` after the list box, outside it and outside the box that scrolls; its text is drawn in a span kept from assistive technology, and two visually hidden spans, `role="status"` and `role="alert"`, are its live regions, always in the shadow root and given the text one animation frame after the list is shown (empty while it is closed), so that what the row already says as the list opens is read. While loading the list box has `aria-busy="true"` and the row holds one `<tanrei-loading-indicator size="small">` named by `status-text`. `empty-text` left empty is read from the product's words (`setWords({ noOptionsText })`). The `inline` attribute, for tests and fixtures, draws the open list in place below the trigger. What belongs to the frame and not to the element: the attributes `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `required`, `optional`, `required-mark`, `required-text`, `optional-text`, the `label-icon` slot, the parts `label-icon` and `supporting-text`, and the label row of the stacked look. In a debug build the element reports any of those six attributes, or a child for `label-icon`, once, and names `tanrei-select-field`: nothing is kept for them in a production build, and no alias exists. Before the element is defined its options are running text in the page; what a server-rendered page shows then is the product's to guard today: hide `tanrei-select:not(:defined) > *` and reserve the block size of the select's size, and where the page must work without script put a native `<select>` or links in a `<noscript>` beside it. The native `<select>` is not used inside: its list cannot be drawn with the system's tokens, groups, glyphs and supporting text. The chevron is the icon helper's `expand_more` and the check its `check`. The clear button (SEL-72) is a `<tanrei-button variant="text" size="small">` after the `role="combobox"` element in the shadow root, placed over the container's end, so that no button is inside the combobox; the container keeps its room with a margin before the chevron. `clear-label` left empty is read from the product's words (`setWords({ clearLabel })`).

swiftui.notes: `TanreiSelect(_ label:, selection: Binding<String>) { TanreiSelectOption("Japan").tag("jp") … }`, shaped as `Picker`: the platform's control of this kind, whose call site and whose accessibility a product expects. SwiftUI's own `Picker` and `Menu` are not used to draw it, for the reason TanreiMenu gives: their lists cannot be drawn with the system's tokens. The trigger is Tanrei's own box; the list is presented as TanreiMenu presents its surface (`.popover` with `presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)`, so it stays anchored on iPhone). Writing the binding is change; `isPresented` is an optional binding, and writing it is toggle. `labelHidden` follows `.labelsHidden()`, `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`. The trigger is one accessibility element with the button trait, the label as its label, the chosen option's label as its value and a pop-up hint; the options are buttons with the selected trait. A press outside does not reach what is under the list. With a hardware keyboard the arrow keys move the highlight and Return chooses, focus staying on the trigger. The bare control: `label` names it where no Field frames it and floats in a filled or outlined look; in a form it stands in `TanreiField`, which is `TanreiSelectField`.

The trigger is Tanrei's own box with `Role.DropdownList`, the label as its content description, the chosen label as its state description and the expanded state; the list is shown in a `Popup` as TanreiMenu's is, its options `selectable` with their selected state inside a `selectableGroup`.
